newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge to invest 7-8 bln Ffr - paper.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge to invest 7-8 bln Ffr - paper.

text.p: French building materials company Lafarge SA expects to invest between seven and eight billion francs in 1996 and the same amount for each of the next two years, chairman Bertrand Collomb said.

"We have planned seven to eight billion francs of investments for 1996 and we will continue at the same rythmn in 1997 and 1998," he said in an interview with weekly Journal des Finances due to appear on Saturday.
That amount should be seen in the light of Lafarge's annual cashflow of four to five billion francs. The company could afford to increase its debt leverage, he said.

"Taking into account the size of our equity capital, 31.6 billion francs at the end of June and our net debt of 4.4 billion francs, we have the ability to increase our debt by a margin of 10 billion francs," Collomb said.
Lafarge's geographical spread will change drastically in five years' time. France, which currently accounts for 32 percent of turnover, will fall relative to other areas.
Collomb did not rule out capital gains by the end of the year.
"There will not be sales of large activities as in last year, but in a group like ours, there are always 'bits' of assets to sell," he said.
He said in a statement with first-half results on Wednesday that the company expected to an improved second half and a full year operating profit similar to last year.
The company reported 1995 year operating profit of 4.04 billion francs and net attributable profit of 2.35 billion francs. -- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
